blocks.content: 13.4 Bru-Reang Refugee Settlement — A Historical Resolution

The Bru (Reang) refugee crisis was one of the longest-standing humanitarian issues in northeast India. The Bru/Reang tribe, originally from Mizoram's Mamit district, fled to Tripura in 1997 following ethnic violence in Mizoram. Approximately 37,000 Bru people lived in relief camps in North Tripura for over 23 years.

items: January 16, 2020: Tripartite agreement signed between Centre, Mizoram, and Tripura; Bru to be permanently settled in Tripura
Settlement package: Each Bru family to receive: 0.03 acres of land, Rs 1.5 lakh cash, Rs 4 lakh for house, free ration for 2 years, and Rs 5,000/month for 2 years
12 settlement locations identified in North Tripura
By 2024: Most families settled; schools, roads, and services being established
Significance: Ends 27-year-long refugee crisis; ensures tribal welfare; shows cooperative federalism
